timeline.first_impact_assessment: The preliminary orbit computation indicated a possible Earth impact within approximately 21 hours of discovery.

observation_snapshot.interpretation: CNEOS reports approximately 570 positional measurements from 26 observatories by the time the object entered Earth's shadow. This is a snapshot count, not the final all-observations total.

preimpact_forecast_summary.publication_snapshot: JPL described publishing an impact announcement at approximately 21:30 UTC on 2008-10-06; this summary time is approximate and must not be used as a precision forecast epoch.

observed_event.coordinate_precision_note: Observed coordinates are rounded to one decimal degree in the CNEOS comparison table.

terminal_event_reconstructions.interpretation: CNEOS Table 1 compares the final trajectory estimate with observed atmospheric entry; the final estimate incorporates data not necessarily available before impact.

observed_event.coordinate_precision_note: Observed coordinates are rounded to one decimal degree in the CNEOS comparison table.

terminal_event_reconstructions.interpretation: The airburst was observed near 37 km altitude; the table values are a terminal reconstruction rather than a clean pre-impact forecast snapshot.

recovery.scope_note: Nature's 2009 report describes 47 recovered meteorites with a combined mass of 3.95 kg; this is the scope of that published campaign, not necessarily every later recovered fragment.

sources.title: Asteroid 2008 TC3 Strikes Earth: Predictions and Observations Agree
2008 TC3 — ESA Near-Earth Object Coordination Centre
The impact and recovery of asteroid 2008 TC3

data_gaps: Raw MPC astrometry records, with exact observation times and source metadata, must be frozen before time-sliced orbit-determination replay.
The numerical terminal predictions in the CNEOS comparison table are final reconstructed values and must not be mislabeled as the pre-impact as-of forecast.
The rounded observed geographic coordinates do not support sub-kilometre residual scoring without original event-location uncertainty and coordinate provenance.
Atmospheric entry and fragmentation models are outside this orbit-prediction reference case.
